subtitle: Lesson 18 · Threat Intelligence & Indicators of Compromise

code:
Threat intelligence feed =
a continuously updated stream
of confirmed-bad IOCs:

malicious IPs, domains,
file hashes -- published by
someone else before the attack
reaches your network.
caption: A feed is thousands of Lesson 17's IOCs, refreshed constantly from outside sources.

steps.label: Commercial vendors
steps.sub: security companies selling curated, high-confidence feeds

steps.label: ISACs
steps.sub: sector-specific groups — finance, healthcare — pooling what members see

steps.label: Open-source projects
steps.sub: research community feeds, often first to publish a new campaign

steps.label: A mature SOC
steps.sub: blends all three — each catches different things first

steps.label: TIP ingests feeds
steps.sub: pulls in multiple sources, deduplicates and scores them

steps.label: Pushes blocklists
steps.sub: sends the result to enforcement points automatically

steps.label: Firewall enforces
steps.sub: any device reaching that IP is blocked before a human looks

steps.label: No manual review needed
steps.sub: defends against infrastructure the SOC has never personally seen

eyebrow: Context an analyst didn't have to research
code:
Bare SIEM alert:
  "Workstation connected to 1 IP"

Enriched with feed context:
  "...reported in 40 orgs' incidents
   this month as Cobalt Strike C2"

Same alert. Very different response time.
caption: Enrichment lets an analyst skip research and go straight to containment.

subtitle: The real standard for sharing threat intel between organizations.
